IND @ MICH • Sat 12:00pm
IND -7
-115
Spread
Picked: Oct 22 @ 6:30pm
Analysis
DraftKings. This number looks like it's headed toward 7.5 at most sportsbooks, so I'll grab Indiana -7 now. The Hoosiers are coming off a rare loss under Curt Cignetti and I don't know how Michigan scores. The Wolverines' defense will keep them in the game for a while, but I see Indiana pulling away at some point. Tommy Carr may be Michigan's long-term answer at QB. However, Carr's problem in his first career start is that Indiana's defense allows just 75 rushing yards per game and 2.28 yards per carry. If Josh Hoover takes care of the football, IU should win this game by double digits. Give me the Hoosiers -7 for one unit.
NCAAF
ALBANY @ RI • Sat 12:00pm
RI
-166
Money Line
Picked: Oct 23 @ 2:34am
Analysis
Rhode Island looked great last Saturday in a blowout road upset win at ranked Yale out of conference and has won both at home thus far, allowing only 20 total points. QB Alex McClelland is the reigning CAA Offensive Player of the Week. Last season, Rhody won this matchup 58-17 away. Pretty much all the game notes tell me other than every player's favorite place to eat in the greater Kingston, R.I. area.
NCAAF
IND @ MICH • Sat 12:00pm
Under 42.5
-105
Over/Under
Picked: Oct 23 @ 12:02pm
Analysis
This is a battle of two of the best defenses in the country and two offenses that have not shown much this season.
Indiana allows just 12.9 points per game, best in the Big Ten and fourth best in the country.
They just held the Ohio State offense to 19 points and 313 total yards, but lost because the offense could only muster 2 TDs and 369 yards.
Michigan's defense is arguably even better, 4th in the nation and first in the Big Ten in yards (256.5), and 19th in scoring at 16.2 PPG, while facing a tougher schedule than Indiana. They've allowed 4.1 yards per play this season, best in the country.
Michigan has allowed 20 points or fewer in all six games.

2026 MLB playoff bracket: Schedule and scores as Brewers take World Series Game 1 over Rays
The Brewers-Rays matchup guarantees that we'll have a first-time champion in 2026
By
Kate Feldman
Oct 23, 2026
at
11:27 pm ET
2 min read
Add CBS Sports on Google
Adam Eargle, CBS Sports Design
The Milwaukee Brewers took a 1-0 World Series lead with a Game 1 win over the Tampa Bay Rays on Friday night. Jacob Misiorowski and the elite Brewers bullpen held the Rays to just two runs despite a late scare, while the offense scraped across just enough for a 3-2 win.
The Rays secured the American League pennant by beating the Cleveland Guardians in ALCS Game 6 behind a massive home run by Junior Caminero. This marks their first World Series appearance since 2020, and only their third in franchise history (they lost to the Philadelphia Phillies in 2008). The Brewers, meanwhile, swept the Los Angeles Dodgers to win the National League pennant and make their first World Series since 1982.
Neither franchise has ever won a title, meaning we'll get a first-time champion regardless of the outcome.

College football schedule 2026: What to watch in Week 8, TV channels, streaming, Saturday kickoff times
Will we see even more college football craziness in Week 8's best games?
By
Austin Nivison
Oct 23, 2026
at
12:47 pm ET
4 min read
Add CBS Sports on Google
Getty Images
Week 8 may not be jam-packed with banger after banger like the Week 7 college football slate, but upsets and season-changing outcomes can happen on any given weekend. There's certainly the possibility for some of that on Saturday.
Fresh off its devastating loss to Ohio State, No. 6 Indiana must travel to Ann Arbor, where it will face one of the best defenses in the Big Ten. Quarterback Josh Hoover seemed to injure his throwing shoulder against the Buckeyes, but he wasn't on the Wednesday night availability report. There's a lot of quarterback uncertainty on the other side with the Wolverines starting a freshman.
Down in Austin, there will be a lot of anxiety as No. 7 Ole Miss faces No. 19 Texas. The Longhorns need a win in the worst way, but they'll have to get one against one of the best quarterbacks in the country, Trinidad Chambliss. If Arch Manning struggles again this week, will Steve Sarkisian turn to KJ Lacey behind center?
Elsewhere around the country, Auburn will try to spring a second consecutive upset with LSU coming to Jordan-Hare Stadium, and No. 15 Iowa will meet Minnesota in a battle for a 98-pound bronze pig.
With so much college football on at once, we've created a viewer's guide to help prioritize your Saturday schedule.
No. 6 Indiana at Michigan -- 12 p.m. on Fox, Fubo (try for free): How does Indiana respond to a gut-wrenching loss to Ohio State? How does freshman quarterback Tommy Carr play in his first career start against the Hoosiers? The Wolverines got a badly needed win over Penn State last week, but that doesn't mean their offensive woes are suddenly fixed. The issue for Indiana is that Josh Hoover hasn't been dialed in over the last two games, and now he has to go on the road to face a very good defense. This could be a low-scoring affair.
No. 18 LSU at Auburn -- 12 p.m. on ABC, Fubo (try for free): LSU has lost eight consecutive road games. Auburn is 1-9 in its last 10 home games against top-25 opponents. Something has to give on Saturday afternoon. After knocking off No. 1 Georgia, Auburn returns home to Jordan-Hare Stadium, and the fans will be fired up to reward that performance in Athens. Can Kiffin and his team finish on the road in a hostile environment -- something they've been unable to do in their two games away from Baton Rouge this fall? There has to be some desperation for LSU because it can't afford a third loss already.
No. 15 Iowa at Minnesota -- 3:30 p.m. on FS1, Fubo (try for free): The Hawkeyes and Golden Gophers are playing for a 98-pound bronze pig this weekend. That should be enough to sell you on this game, but there is intrigue beyond the pork prize. Iowa is off to a tremendous start, and the offense was extremely efficient with Jeremy Hecklinski at quarterback against Washington. Minnesota has an opportunity to reach 3-1 in conference play with a win at home, but the Golden Gophers have been inconsistent there so far.
No. 7 Ole Miss at No. 19 Texas -- 7:30 p.m. on ABC, Fubo (try for free): Puckering may be at an all-time high in Austin this weekend. Texas is trying to avoid a third consecutive loss, but here comes seventh-ranked Ole Miss and Trinidad Chambliss. Arch Manning hasn't been benched, but KJ Lacey will get more first-team reps in practice this week. Oh, and Colin Simmons is listed as doubtful on the availability report. Yet, the Longhorns are favored to win this game. If they can pull out a win, the schedule gets a little more favorable for at least a couple of weeks.
NDSU at New Mexico -- 10 p.m. on CW, Fubo (try for free): Brew a pot of coffee and stay up late for this one. Jason Eck is doing sketch comedy to pack University Stadium, and NDSU wants to make a huge statement on the road. Welcome to the new Mountain West. It's a glorious league. The winner of this game will have the inside track to a conference title and absolutely has to be considered for the College Football Playoff. And, if the Lobos win, Eck's profile will only rise amongst teams that might be in the market for a new coach.

The Cougars just notched a top-25 win over Oklahoma State, and they went toe-to-toe with Texas Tech in Lubbock. The Utes, on the other hand, haven't exactly been tested so far. That will change on Saturday, and the matchup between Utah's defense and Houston's offense will be fascinating. The former looked shaky at times against Colorado and Kansas, but the latter has sputtered against the better defenses on its schedule.

2026 WNBA playoffs bracket, WNBA Finals schedule: Dream take Game 3 vs. Valkyries
The Dream and Valkyries are battling in the 2026 WNBA Finals and Atlanta now holds a 2-1 lead
By
Lindsay Gibbs
Oct 22, 2026
at
12:02 am ET
2 min read
Add CBS Sports on Google
Adam Eargle, CBS Sports
The Atlanta Dream took a 2-1 lead over the Golden State Valkyries in the WNBA Finals with a Game 3 win on Wednesday night. Angel Reese scored a game-high 21 points in the win and was one of five Dream players to score in double figures.
The series resumes on Saturday in Atlanta as the Dream host Game 4. Both teams are looking to win a title for the first time in franchise history.
The Dream and Valkyries both completed semifinal sweeps, giving them a week off before the Finals. Atlanta knocked out the New York Liberty, while Golden State ousted the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces.
The Dream knocked the Washington Mystics out in the first round and are a perfect 5-0 in the playoffs. The Valkyries defeated the Dallas Wings in the first round, needing all three games to do so. The Finals, for the second season ever, are a best-of-seven series in 2026.
The 2026 WNBA season has been groundbreaking, on and off the court. It launched on the heels of a contentious and extended labor battle that resulted in a historic raise for the players (the salary cap increased from $1.5 million in 2025 to $7 million in 2026), and in return, the players raised the bar on a weekly basis. Multiple regular-season records fell this year, from Clark becoming the first player in WNBA history with a 40-point, 10-assist game, to Angel Reese breaking the single-game rebounding record with 26 to Kelsey Mitchell passing A'ja Wilson's single-season points record.

For the first time all season, it feels like we may get more players back this week than we lost last week. Part of that may be the fact that the Lions and Bengals are coming off a bye. Another part is that far fewer players played last week and suffered a significant injury. That's fantastic news. What is also fantastic is that the running back position may get some much-needed depth added, even if we aren't sure we're getting them all the way back in Week 7.
As of Monday evening, we are projecting Josh Jacobs and Zach Charbonnet to make their season debuts this week. Both Green Bay and Seattle have struggled running the ball this season, which is both a blessing and a curse for their returning starters. The blessing is that Jacobs and Charbonnet should get as much work as they can handle moving forward. The curse is that it is hard to project them as very efficient, given how these lines have been blocking.
For Week 7, it is best to view both as high-end flexes who could be RB2s if they score a touchdown. I have both Jacobs and Charbonnet projected for double-digit touches, but just barely. Jacobs has a better chance at a touchdown because he is facing the Lions, while Charbonnet gets the Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. We're also projecting Quinshon Judkins to return from his ankle injury, and would start him over both.
Prominent players, we had projected last week that we are not projecting to play in Week 6 as of Monday evening:

UFC 333 presents two of the year's most compelling title fights: a first-time clash between Alexander Volkanovski and Movsar Evloev, and the last stop in Petr Yan and Merab Dvalishvili's trilogy. Their stories unravel in Abu Dhabi on Saturday.
Volkanovski is savoring the closing chapters of his legendary career. Already a two-time featherweight champion, arguably the greatest his division has seen, he builds on that legacy with every successful title defense. However, Volkanovski's status as an all-time great is assured, and he's prepared to hang it up if things go disastrously. He doesn't expect that to happen this weekend. Volkanovski has all the respect in the world for Evloev, but believes the title challenger is at a stark stylistic disadvantage.

It's a big Texas weekend. There are only two ranked games featuring top-25 teams in Week 8, and each involves a Texas school.
No. 7 Ole Miss travels to No. 19 Texas (7:30 p.m. ET) in what feels like a referendum game for both Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian and starting quarterback Arch Manning. The narratives have gone into overdrive this week as Texas has lost its last two games, both to unranked opponents, as the Manning-led Texas offense has struggled mightily. Rust? What rust? Brewers open World Series refreshed and ready thanks to all that winning
The Brewers have now played nine games in the last 26 days and they've won eight of them
By
Matt Snyder
Oct 24, 2026
at
12:18 am ET
6 min read
Add CBS Sports on Google
Getty Images
MILWAUKEE -- The Milwaukee Brewers won Game 1 of the World Series, 3-2, Friday night at American Family Field. It was their first win since Thursday, Oct. 15. They hadn't lost since then either, though; they had been off.
Any time a team has a long layoff in the postseason, we end up hearing the same tired song and dance. "Rust vs. Rest" is the succinct headline. The basic argument is that with baseball being a daily sport in the regular season, teams sitting around for multiple days between series -- or between the end of the regular season and the divisional series -- are at some sort of disadvantage because they'll come out rusty.
It's nonsense, of course.
One example obviously doesn't disprove a theory -- though we have several more and we'll get to those -- but the Brewers are doing their best to kill that narrative.
In the first inning of World Series Game 1 on Friday, Jackson Chourio led off with a single. Christian Yelich tripled him home and then scored on a William Contreras single. In the span of four batters, the team that spent seven full days without playing a game just scored two runs. Nick Martinez, on the mound for the Rays, wasn't great in the second half, but he was an All-Star this season and was coming off an outing in which he allowed only one run in more than five innings against the Guardians in the ALCS.
Was Contreras rusty? After that RBI single in the first, he threw out two runners trying to steal and nailed both of his ABS challenges. It sure seems like a rusty catcher wouldn't be so excellent behind the plate at judging balls and strikes.
"Contreras was unbelievable," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said after the game. "The two caught stealings, the ABS, the hits, calling the game.
" ... Now, we did not play great. You can look back and we made a baserunning mistake, we made an execution mistake. We made a defensive mistake. We weren't perfect. But after being off for some time, I'm pleased we came out in the first inning ready to go."
The wait between sweeping the Dodgers in the NLDS and Game 1 of the World Series wasn't the Brewers' only break. They have now played just nine games in 26 days. They've won eight of them. It sort of blows up that "rusty" argument, doesn't it?
As all teams with long layoffs do, the Brewers had plenty of practices. These days, that's not just swings off batting practice pitchers; Trajekt technology uses holograms of real pitchers and recreates everything about their pitches, including spin rate, velocity, movement, the works. The tech has gotten so good that players have started bypassing minor-league rehab assignments after injury absences and instead just getting back up to game speed using the Trajekt machines.
The Brewers also played practice games.
"We played baseball, that's how we prepared," Murphy said on Thursday before their team workout. "We went out there and played baseball every day, live at-bats. You can't recreate real, you know what I mean? It's a long layoff, and if we want to use it as an excuse, then let people use it as an excuse, but I refuse to do that."
I'm glad he said something about excuses, because some of the narratives we've seen used with teams after layoffs in the past are tantamount to excuse-making. When high-seeded teams lose a game or even a series, people love to cling to excuses instead of just accepting that baseball in small samples lends itself to variance.
Sure, we've heard former players making claims like your body doesn't adjust well to not playing games for multiple days after having played nearly every day for six months, and maybe they do feel that, but the numbers tell us otherwise.
The 2022 and 2023 Braves seemed to be the poster child for this under the current playoff format, which debuted in 2022. How many times did we hear about how unfair it was that the top two seeds were forced to sit around and get rusty while the lower seeds get to play meaningful baseball, giving them a supposed edge?
Rubbish. Utter rubbish.
That very argument ignored the top-seeded Astros in 2022. They got a bye and then swept the Mariners in the ALDS, waited a few more days off and then swept the Yankees in the ALCS. They had another long layoff before the World Series and then beat the Phillies six games. They went 11-2 in all, the best record in this iteration of the playoffs. If the Brewers sweep here, they'll beat it.
In the current playoff format, teams with at least five days of rest before Game 1 have gone 14-10 in Games 1. You might think 10 losses is too many, but that record is a 162-game pace of 95 wins, and these are obviously all games against playoff teams. The rested teams are good, not rusty.
Let's get back to the Brewers. They earned the spotlight just as they've been doing all playoffs and, really, nearly the entire season. They earned the rest during their bye by having the best record in baseball with 103 wins. They earned their days off before the NLCS by getting rid of the Padres in four games instead of five. They earned more than a week of rest before the World Series by taking out the two-time defending champion Dodgers in a four-game sweep.

A big night of fights is set to go down in Abu Dhabi on Saturday. The UFC 333 card is headlined by a pair of title fights, including undefeated Movsar Evloev challenging Alexander Volkanovski for the UFC featherweight championship in the main event.
Evloev holds a perfect 20-0 professional record, but he'll face the biggest test of his career in Volkanovski, who is on his second run as 145-pound champion at age 38.
In the co-main event, Petr Yan and Merab Dvalishvili will clash in a rubber match for the bantamweight championship. Dvalishvili won their first meeting en route to winning the championship and a lengthy title run, but dropped the belt to Yan in their December rematch.

The rest of the main card has more evenly matched fights that could provide some answers for key divisions as the end of the year approaches. A pair of young and exciting flyweights meet in a featured bout when Lone'er Kavanagh takes on Ramazan Temirov. Plus, perennial heavyweight contender Alexander Volkov looks to put a final stamp on his contendership when he takes on Rizvan Kuniev in a key battle. And former top prospect Aaron Pico looks to take the next step in his rise when he faces knockout artist Losene Keita at featherweight.

Alexander Volkanovski vs. Movsar Evloev predictions
Campbell: Volkanovski's longevity has been remarkable to see, especially after he bounced back from stoppage losses to Islam Makhachev and Ilia Topuria to regain the featherweight title. But it must be said that both of his victories since those damaging defeats came against the all-action but technically limited Diego Lopes, whom Evloev defeated by decision in 2023. For whatever Evloev lacks as a finisher inside the Octagon, he has size, an incredible motor and a physical grappling style that has the potential to wear down the 38-year-old Volkanovski in the championship rounds. He also has a better fight IQ than what Lopes showed against Volkanovski over 10 rounds.
Brookhouse: There are few fights where I will pick against Volkanovski until I've truly seen time catch up to him. Evloev has tremendous wrestling and a willingness to use that wrestling to grind out ugly wins, but Volkanovski has a well-rounded game that also features strong takedown defense. Volkanovski has been here before and he's got the kind of gritty, gutsy game that should require Evloev to do more than just wrestle. While Evloev has shown some strong skills when forced to fight on the feet, Volkanovski has brilliant timing and distance management tools that should let him edge out the fight on the cards.
Mahjouri: Volkanovski says he'll deliver such a sublime performance that fans will think he's de-aged. I'm inclined to believe him. The champion doesn't mean to disrespect his challenger. In fact, he believes Evloev is supremely talented. Volkanovski's confidence stems from the style matchup. He sharpened his grappling defense in preparation for two lightweight fights with Islam Makhachev. On the feet, it's his fight to lose.
